label: prf:q-gaussian-obstruction-at-q0
title: Proof of q gaussian obstruction at q0
html:
Proof

Step 1 — maximal crossings. A perfect matching of [2n] has at most \binom{n}{2} crossings, attained by M^\star = \{(i,\, n+i) : 1 \le i \le n\}. For i < j \le n the arcs interleave, i < j < n+i < n+j, so all \binom{n}{2} arc-pairs cross; and no matching can exceed \binom{n}{2} because that is the total number of arc-pairs. (Confirmed by exhaustive enumeration for n \le 6: \max_\pi \mathrm{cr}(\pi) = \binom{n}{2}, achieved by M^\star.)

Step 2 — super-exponential lower bound. Each summand q_0^{\mathrm{cr}(\pi)} is positive, so retaining only the M^\star term,

  T_n(q_0) \;\ge\; q_0^{\binom{n}{2}}
  \;=\; \exp\!\Big( \tfrac{n(n-1)}{2}\,\ln q_0 \Big)
  \;=\; \exp\!\big(\Theta(n^2)\big),

since \ln q_0 > 0. The exponent is quadratic in n, so T_n(q_0) outgrows c^{\,n} for every constant c — super-exponential divergence. (The exact values T_n(q_0) = 3.11,\,16.7,\,131,\,1365,\,1.81\!\times\!10^4,\, 2.96\!\times\!10^5 for n=2,\dots,7 confirm a ratio T_n/T_{n-1} that grows with n rather than saturating, the signature of \exp(\Theta(n^2)).)

Step 3 — no probability measure. By Bożejko–Speicher, the q-deformed commutation relations a_i a_j^{\dagger} - q\, a_j^{\dagger} a_i = \delta_{ij} admit a positive (Fock-space) representation iff -1 \le q \le 1. At q_0 > 1 the associated Gram form fails to be positive semi-definite, so no q-Gaussian state — hence no representing probability measure — exists; the moment blow-up of Step 2 is the concrete witness (T_n outgrows the moment sequence of any measure with a finite analytic moment-generating function). \square
